en: in the manner of moving an inch

examples.ko: 지하철이 너무 붐벼서 옴짝달싹 못 했어요.
examples.en: The subway was so crowded that I couldn't move an inch.

examples.ko: 아기가 팔을 잡혀서 옴짝달싹도 못 하고 울었어요.
examples.en: The baby had its arms held and cried, unable to budge.

examples.ko: 눈이 너무 많이 와서 차들이 옴짝달싹 못 하고 서 있어요.
examples.en: It snowed so much that the cars are standing still, unable to move.

examples.ko: 약속이 꽉 차서 이번 주에는 옴짝달싹할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: My schedule is so full that I can't budge this week.

examples.ko: 빚 때문에 옴짝달싹 못 하는 처지가 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of debt, I ended up in a situation where I can't make a move.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 노려보는 바람에 옴짝달싹 못 하고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: He glared at me, so I just stood there, frozen.

explain: 거의 항상 '못 하다', '없다' 같은 부정과 함께 써요. 비슷한 말로 '꼼짝'이 있고, '꼼짝도 못 하다'처럼 말해요. 몸이 움직이지 못할 때뿐 아니라 빚이나 일 때문에 상황이 막혔을 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative such as '못 하다' or '없다'. A similar word is '꼼짝', as in '꼼짝도 못 하다'. It is used not only when your body can't move but also when debt or work leaves you stuck.

examples.en: Tying the otgoreum on a hanbok is difficult.
The otgoreum on my jeogori came undone, so I tied it again.

examples.ko: 할머니가 제 한복 옷고름을 예쁘게 매 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother tied the otgoreum on my hanbok nicely for me.
I learned how to tie an otgoreum at the museum.
My otgoreum almost came loose while I was dancing.

examples.ko: 옷고름 색이 치마 색과 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The color of the otgoreum goes well with the skirt.

explain: '옷고름을 매다', '옷고름을 풀다'처럼 '매다', '풀다'와 같이 써요. 옷마다 짝이 되는 동사가 달라서 단추는 '채우다', 지퍼는 '올리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '매다' (to tie) and '풀다' (to undo), as in '옷고름을 매다'. Each kind of fastener has its own verb: buttons are '채우다' and zippers are '올리다'.

examples.ko: 면접 전에 거울 앞에서 옷매무새를 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before the interview, I checked how my clothes looked in front of a mirror.

examples.ko: 사진 찍기 전에 옷매무새를 한번 고쳤어요.
examples.en: I straightened my clothes once before the photo was taken.
The wind messed up how my clothes looked.

examples.ko: 선생님이 학생들에게 옷매무새를 단정히 하라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told the students to tidy up their clothes.
Before going up to present, I checked my clothes first.
He always looks neat in his clothes.

explain: '옷차림'이 입은 옷 전체의 모습이라면, '옷매무새'는 옷을 입고 나서 매만진 맵시나 단정함을 말해요. '옷매무새를 고치다', '옷매무새가 흐트러지다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '옷차림' is the overall look of what you wear, while '옷매무새' focuses on how neatly the clothes are put on and arranged. Common patterns are '옷매무새를 고치다' (to straighten one's clothes) and '옷매무새가 흐트러지다' (to look disheveled).

examples.ko: 할아버지는 옹고집이라서 한번 정하면 안 바꿔요.
examples.en: My grandfather is so pigheaded that once he decides, he never changes.

examples.ko: 옹고집을 부리지 말고 친구 얘기도 들어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't be stubborn, and listen to your friend too.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 옹고집 때문에 회의가 길어졌어요.
examples.en: The meeting got long because of his pigheadedness.

examples.ko: 저는 옹고집이 센 편이라서 양보를 잘 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm rather pigheaded, so I'm not good at giving in.
The employees are having a hard time because of their pigheaded boss.
The child's stubbornness is just like his dad's.

explain: '고집'과 비슷하지만 더 억지스럽고 답답한 느낌이 있어서 흉볼 때 많이 써요. '옹고집을 부리다'처럼 말하고, 그냥 '고집을 부리다/피우다/세다'도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is similar to '고집' but feels more unreasonable and frustrating, so it is often used when criticizing someone. Say '옹고집을 부리다'; it also helps to know '고집을 부리다/피우다' and '고집이 세다'.

examples.en: This year the apples grew in nice and solid.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 몸집은 작아도 속이 옹골차요.
examples.en: That child is small, but solid on the inside.
I came up to Seoul with a solid dream.
The players went into the game with firm determination.

examples.ko: 이 세트는 구성이 옹골차서 가격보다 훨씬 만족스러워요.
examples.en: This set is so well packed that it's far more satisfying than its price.
He lived his life with substance, so I respect him.

explain: '알차다', '야무지다'와 비슷해요. 사람의 단단하고 야무진 모습에도, 내용이 꽉 찬 물건에도 써요. '옹골차요/옹골찬/옹골차게'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It is close to '알차다' and '야무지다'. It describes a person who is firm and capable, and also things that are packed with substance. Typical forms are '옹골차요', '옹골찬', and '옹골차게'.

examples.en: I scooped up water and drank it at a small spring in the mountains.
The water from the small spring is very clear and cool.
I found a small spring while hiking.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할머니 댁 뒷산에 옹달샘이 있었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, there was a small spring on the hill behind my grandmother's house.
Let's rest for a moment in front of the spring before we go.
I was curious about the spring in the children's song, so I looked it up.

explain: '우물'은 사람이 땅을 파서 만들지만, 옹달샘은 산이나 숲에서 물이 저절로 솟아요. 그냥 '샘'보다 작고 오목해서 아담한 느낌이 들어요. 동요 가사 '깊은 산속 옹달샘' 덕분에 한국 사람들에게 친숙해요.
explain_en: A '우물' (well) is dug by people, but an 옹달샘 wells up by itself in the mountains or woods. It is smaller and shallower than a plain '샘', so it feels cozy. Koreans know it well from the children's song lyric '깊은 산속 옹달샘'.

examples.en: My salary is small, so we're badly off.

examples.ko: 방이 옹색해서 짐을 둘 곳이 없어요.
examples.en: The room is so cramped that there's no place for my things.
Even as an excuse, that's really lame.
Even in a cramped house, the family lived laughing.

examples.ko: 돈 때문에 옹색하게 사는 게 싫어요.
examples.en: I hate living on a tight budget because of money.

examples.ko: 사정이 옹색해도 아이 교육만큼은 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even though we were hard up, we didn't give up on our child's education.

explain: 돈이 없어서 형편이 어렵거나 공간이 좁아서 답답할 때 써요. '변명이 옹색하다'처럼 말이 궁색할 때도 쓰는데, '궁색하다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: It describes tight finances or a cramped, stuffy space. It is also used for weak, lame words, as in '변명이 옹색하다', which is close to '궁색하다'.

examples.ko: 우리 아기가 요즘 방긋 웃으며 옹알이해요.
examples.en: These days our baby smiles brightly and babbles.
The baby started babbling when it saw its mom.
At about how many months do babies usually start babbling?

examples.ko: 옹알이하는 모습이 너무 귀여워서 영상을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The baby was so cute babbling that I took a video.

examples.ko: 아기가 혼자 장난감을 보며 옹알이하고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is babbling by itself while looking at a toy.
My nephew was babbling and suddenly fell asleep.

explain: 말을 배우기 전의 아기가 내는 소리에만 써요. 어른이 중얼거릴 때는 쓰지 않아요. '옹알이를 하다'처럼 명사 '옹알이'로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used only for the sounds a baby makes before learning to talk, never for an adult mumbling. People also often say '옹알이를 하다' using the noun '옹알이'.

examples.ko: 그렇게 사소한 일로 화내는 건 옹졸해요.
examples.en: Getting angry over such a trivial thing is petty.

examples.ko: 저는 마음이 옹졸한 사람이 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to become a narrow-minded person.

examples.ko: 친구가 잘돼서 질투하다니 제가 너무 옹졸했어요.
examples.en: I was so petty to be jealous of my friend's success.

examples.ko: 옹졸하게 굴지 말고 한 번만 봐줘요.
examples.en: Don't be petty, just let it go this once.

examples.ko: 그 상사는 옹졸해서 작은 실수도 잊지 않아요.
examples.en: That boss is petty and never forgets even small mistakes.
Drop the narrow thinking and look at the big picture.

explain: '속이 좁다'와 비슷한데, '옹졸하다'가 조금 더 딱딱한 말이에요. 사람의 마음이나 태도에 써요. 반대말은 '너그럽다', '대범하다'예요.
explain_en: It is similar to '속이 좁다', but '옹졸하다' sounds a bit more formal. It is used for a person's mind or attitude. Its opposites are '너그럽다' and '대범하다'.

examples.en: I got a lacquer rash, and my whole body itches.
My arms turned red, maybe from a lacquer rash I got in the mountains.

examples.ko: 옻 때문에 병원에 가야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I have to go to the hospital because of the lacquer.
I'm sensitive to lacquer, so I'm careful.

examples.ko: 옻이 올랐을 때는 긁지 말고 병원에 가세요.
examples.en: When you get a lacquer rash, don't scratch it, go to the doctor.

examples.ko: 옻으로 칠한 그릇은 오래 써도 윤이 나요.
examples.en: Bowls painted with lacquer stay shiny even after long use.

explain: '옻이 오르다', '옻을 타다'가 가장 흔한 표현이에요. 옻나무를 만지거나 옻으로 만든 음식을 먹고 피부가 가려워질 때 말해요.
explain_en: The most common expressions are '옻이 오르다' and '옻을 타다'. They are used when your skin gets itchy after touching lacquer trees or eating food made with them.

examples.ko: 이 밥상은 옻칠을 해서 윤기가 나요.
examples.en: This dining table is lacquered, so it has a gloss.
Lacquerware crafts are quite expensive.

examples.ko: 장인이 몇 번이나 옻칠을 덧발라서 완성했어요.
examples.en: The master craftsman finished it by applying lacquer over and over.
I heard that lacquered bowls hold up well against water.
They explained the lacquering technique at the museum.

examples.ko: 오래된 가구에 옻칠을 다시 하려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm going to lacquer the old furniture again.

explain: '옻칠을 하다'라고 말하고, '옻칠한 그릇'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸며 줘요. 나전칠기 같은 전통 공예 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Say '옻칠을 하다', and it can modify a noun, as in '옻칠한 그릇'. It often comes up when talking about traditional crafts such as 나전칠기 (mother-of-pearl lacquerware).

examples.en: The market is swarming with people.
The classroom was so noisy that it was hard to start the lesson.
I can't stand places where bugs are swarming.
During breaks, the hallway is buzzing with kids.
Reporters were crowding noisily in front of the venue.
It was vacation time, so the amusement park was teeming with people.

explain: 사람이나 벌레가 한곳에 많이 모여서 시끄럽게 움직일 때 써요. '붐비다'는 소리가 없어도 쓰지만, 이 말은 시끌시끌한 느낌이 있어요. '와글와글'과 같은 계열의 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when many people or bugs gather in one place and move around noisily. '붐비다' can be used even without noise, but this word carries a buzzing, noisy feel. It belongs to the same family as '와글와글'.

examples.en: Kids are chattering noisily on the playground.

examples.ko: 교실 안이 와글와글해서 선생님 목소리가 안 들려요.
examples.en: The classroom is so noisy that I can't hear the teacher's voice.
The market is bustling every weekend.
This restaurant is too packed and noisy, so let's go somewhere else.

examples.ko: 콘서트장 밖에서 팬들이 와글와글 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Fans are gathered noisily outside the concert hall.
When vacation ended, the school became noisy and lively again.

explain: '와글와글 떠들다'처럼 부사로도 쓰고 '교실이 와글와글하다'처럼 서술어로도 써요. 사람이 많고 시끄러운 장면에 어울려요. '조용하다'가 반대말이에요.
explain_en: It works as an adverb ('와글와글 떠들다') and as a predicate ('교실이 와글와글하다'). It suits scenes with many people and lots of noise. Its opposite is '조용하다'.

examples.en: I waited for the bus shivering from the cold.

examples.ko: 무서운 영화를 보다가 손이 와들와들 떨렸어요.
examples.en: My hands trembled while I was watching a scary movie.

examples.ko: 발표 직전에 다리가 와들와들 떨려서 서 있기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Right before the presentation my legs were shaking so much it was hard to stand.

examples.ko: 와들와들 떨지 말고 이 담요를 덮어요.
examples.en: Stop shivering and cover yourself with this blanket.

examples.ko: 개가 천둥소리에 놀라서 와들와들 떨고 있어요.
examples.en: The dog is startled by the thunder and trembling.

examples.ko: 차가운 물에 들어갔더니 온몸이 와들와들 떨려요.
examples.en: I went into the cold water and my whole body is shivering.

explain: 추위, 두려움, 긴장 때문에 몸이 떨리는 모양이에요. '덜덜'도 비슷하고, '벌벌'은 주로 겁이 나서 떠는 느낌이 강해요. 모두 '떨다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: It describes the body shaking from cold, fear, or nervousness. '덜덜' is similar, and '벌벌' leans more toward trembling from fear. All of them go with '떨다'.

en: all of a sudden; all at once

examples.en: The child ran over and threw its arms around its mom.
As soon as I saw my friend, tears burst out.

examples.ko: 갑자기 와락 겁이 나서 뒤를 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: Suddenly I got scared all at once and looked behind me.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 손을 와락 잡았어요.
examples.en: He grabbed my hand all of a sudden.
The feeling of missing them rushed over me.
My younger sibling lunged at me suddenly and I was startled.

explain: 갑자기 힘 있게 움직이거나 감정이 확 올라올 때 써요. '안다', '잡다', '달려들다', '쏟아지다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 눈물이나 감정에는 '왈칵'도 써요.
explain_en: It is used for a sudden, forceful movement or a surge of emotion. It often appears with '안다', '잡다', '달려들다', and '쏟아지다'. For tears or feelings, '왈칵' is also used.

en: enduring hardship to achieve a goal (lit. sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall)

examples.en: After enduring hardship, he won the championship again.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 작년 패배를 잊지 않고 와신상담했어요.
examples.en: Our team didn't forget last year's defeat and bore the hardship to prepare for revenge.

examples.ko: 와신상담하는 마음으로 시험을 다시 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm preparing for the exam again with a determined, never-give-up spirit.

examples.ko: 몇 년간 와신상담한 끝에 가게를 다시 열었어요.
examples.en: After years of gritting his teeth, he reopened the shop.
The news described it as 'a time of enduring hardship'.
I learned the four-character idiom about enduring hardship to win back what was lost in class.

explain: 실패나 패배를 잊지 않고 고생을 견디며 다시 일어설 날을 기다린다는 뜻의 사자성어예요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '와신상담 끝에'처럼 자주 보이고, '와신상담하다'로도 써요. 비슷한 말로 '절치부심'이 있어요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom describes remembering a failure or defeat and enduring hardship while waiting for the chance to rise again. It often appears in sports news as '와신상담 끝에', and can also be used as '와신상담하다'. A similar idiom is '절치부심'.

examples.en: The plate fell and smashed with a crash.
The window shattered with a loud crash.
The shelf collapsed with a crash and I was startled.
A cat passing by knocked a cup down with a crash.
I heard a crash and ran to the kitchen.

examples.ko: 화분이 와장창 넘어지는 소리에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up at the sound of a flowerpot crashing over.

explain: 물건이 한꺼번에 깨지거나 무너질 때 나는 요란한 소리예요. '쨍그랑'은 유리나 그릇이 깨지는 소리에 주로 쓰고, '와장창'은 더 크고 여러 개가 무너지는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is the loud sound of things breaking or collapsing all at once. '쨍그랑' is mainly the sound of glass or dishes breaking, while '와장창' feels bigger and more like many things falling apart.

examples.ko: 말이 여러 사람을 거치면 와전되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: When words pass through many people, they easily get distorted.

examples.ko: 전해 들은 이야기는 와전됐을 수도 있으니 직접 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: A secondhand story may have been distorted, so check it yourself.

examples.ko: 소문이 와전돼서 제가 회사를 그만둔다고 알려졌어요.
examples.en: The rumor got twisted, and it became known that I was quitting the company.

examples.ko: 제 말이 와전된 것 같아서 해명하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I think my words were misreported, and I want to explain.

examples.ko: 기사 내용이 와전돼 퍼지는 바람에 오해가 생겼어요.
examples.en: The article's content spread in a distorted form, which caused a misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 이야기가 와전되지 않게 메모로 남겨 둘게요.
examples.en: I'll leave it in a note so the story doesn't get distorted.

explain: 말이나 소문이 전해지는 동안 사실과 다르게 바뀔 때 써요. 일부러 거짓말을 만든다기보다 전달되는 과정에서 달라지는 느낌이에요. 쉬운 말로는 '잘못 전해지다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when words or rumors change and no longer match the facts while being passed along. It suggests change during transmission rather than deliberate lying. An easier way to say it is '잘못 전해지다'.

examples.ko: 가게 안이 왁자지껄 시끄러워서 대화가 안 돼요.
examples.en: The shop is so boisterous that we can't have a conversation.
The kids came out of the school gate chattering loudly.

examples.ko: 명절이라 온 가족이 모여 왁자지껄 웃고 떠들어요.
examples.en: It's a holiday, so the whole family gathers and laughs and chats noisily.
The market alley is full of boisterous energy.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 분식집에서 학생들이 왁자지껄 이야기해요.
examples.en: Students are talking noisily at the snack shop in front of the school.
The noisy sounds I'd been hearing suddenly went quiet.

explain: 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 떠드는 소리가 크게 들릴 때 써요. '시끌벅적'과 비슷하고, 즐겁고 활기찬 분위기에 자주 어울려요. 뒤에 '떠들다', '웃다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.
explain_en: It is used when the noise of many people talking at once is loud. It is close to '시끌벅적' and often fits a cheerful, lively atmosphere. Verbs such as '떠들다' and '웃다' often follow it.

examples.en: The market is so noisy that I have to raise my voice.
On holidays the house is lively and noisy.
We ate dinner in a boisterous atmosphere.

examples.ko: 옆 테이블이 너무 왁자지껄해서 이야기하기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The next table was so loud that it was hard to talk.
The noisy classroom went quiet when the teacher walked in.
The classroom is so noisy, so I'll close the window.

explain: '왁자지껄한 분위기', '왁자지껄하던 교실'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미거나 '~이 왁자지껄하다'로 써요. 반대말은 '조용하다'예요. 사람들이 많이 모여 시끄러운 장면에 써요.
explain_en: It can modify a noun, as in '왁자지껄한 분위기' and '왁자지껄하던 교실', or be used as '~이 왁자지껄하다'. Its opposite is '조용하다'. It is used for scenes where many people have gathered and it is loud.

examples.en: My father firmly opposed my marriage.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 끝까지 잘못을 인정하지 않고 완강했어요.
examples.en: He was obstinate and never admitted his mistake to the end.

examples.ko: 정부는 협상 조건을 바꾸지 않겠다는 입장이 완강해요.
examples.en: The government is firm in its position of not changing the negotiation terms.
Faced with his stubborn refusal, I couldn't persuade him any further.

examples.ko: 아이가 병원에 가기 싫다고 완강하게 버텼어요.
examples.en: The child held out stubbornly, saying he didn't want to go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 노조의 요구에 회사 측은 완강한 태도를 보였어요.
examples.en: The company showed an obstinate attitude toward the union's demands.

explain: '고집이 세다'보다 딱딱한 말이라 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. '완강하게 반대하다/거부하다/저항하다', '완강한 태도'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 마음을 쉽게 바꾸지 않는 모습을 나타내요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '고집이 세다', so it often appears in news and writing. It is commonly used in '완강하게 반대하다/거부하다/저항하다' and '완강한 태도'. It describes someone who won't easily change their mind.
